clue.text: Vote to get extra large notice dismantled

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the bat touching the ball
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart, so the letters of notice are pulled to pieces and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone casts a vote to have an oversized public notice taken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismantled' rearranges NOTICE into ECTION. BYE is a cricket extra: a run scored without the batter hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-election is a special poll held between general elections to fill a vacant seat, so it is a kind of vote.

clue.text: Eating bit of chicken?

parts.note: not a portion of chicken to be eaten, but the part a bird eats with

explanation.surface: Someone is eating a piece of chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a morsel of chicken meat; the clue means the part of the bird that does the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's horny mouth is the part it pecks and feeds with, its eating bit.

clue.text: Parts of cereal crop burning in distance we hear

parts.note: ears are the grain-bearing heads of cereal plants
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: Parts of a cereal crop are on fire somewhere within hearing distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The range within which sound can be heard is the distance over which we hear.

clue.text: Continental marriage? It's hard to get out of it!

definitions.text: Continental marriage? It's hard to get out of it!

parts.words: Continental marriage? It's hard to get out of it
parts.note: a political union of nations on the Continent, which Britain found hard to leave

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a European wedding is very hard to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The marriage is a union of countries in mainland Europe; the exclamation alludes to Brexit, Britain's long and difficult departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A union of mainland states is a continental marriage, and Britain's exit from the bloc proved long and hard.

clue.text: Cheers! Whisky with less water is cheaper

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, as is cheers
Whisky is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter W
having less water means being more dry

explanation.surface: A toast with whisky that has less water in it is cheaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'cheers' and TA both mean thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means cheap and showy, so the comparative is cheaper in the sense of more tacky.

clue.text: One gawps, regarding learner driver with turn coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters run bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: re means about or regarding
L is the plate a British learner driver displays
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone stares as a learner driver comes up to a turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses RE + L + GO in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leers or stares lustfully gawps at the object of attention.

clue.text: One's precious ring, left by father

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone treasures a ring that their late father left them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by father' puts L after PA. 'One's precious' reads as a sentimental comment, but it defines a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone is a precious stone, and this iridescent milky gem is one example.

clue.text: Slate and pine — that's style

parts.note: to slate a play is to criticise it harshly, to pan it
to pine for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Slate and pine are stylish materials for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' and 'pine' look like building materials but are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence and flair is a kind of style.

clue.text: China used by pub meeting for Fulham and Chelsea perhaps

definitions.text: meeting for Fulham and Chelsea perhaps

indicators.note: the china comes after the pub, as if used by it

parts.note: your local is the pub nearest your home
Derby is a fine English porcelain, as in Royal Crown Derby

explanation.surface: A pub's crockery is used at a meeting of two football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham and Chelsea are neighbouring London football clubs, so their match is a game between nearby rivals. Derby is a famous English porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A match between two neighbouring clubs is called by this name, and Fulham and Chelsea are near each other in west London.

clue.text: Flying squad character joins prison guards, not taking sides

parts.note: air in the sense of manner or bearing, a person's character as others see it

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its outer letters, so the two ends are dropped from the guards

parts.note: screws is British slang for prison warders

explanation.surface: A police Flying Squad officer teams up with prison warders, staying neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' removes the outer S's from SCREWS, leaving CREW. 'Flying squad' suggests the London police unit, but it means a team who fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff on board an aircraft form a team that works while flying, a literal reading of flying squad.

clue.text: Short cloak, cool — no itch when used off and on

indicators.note: using letters off and on means skipping every other one, so alternate letters are taken from the run of words

explanation.surface: A short, cool cloak that doesn't itch, worn only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when used off and on' takes the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on from CLOAK COOL NO ITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, so it is short or terse.

clue.text: Kitty used by a merchant wandering round eastern region for customers?

indicators.note: the cat comes first, followed by the trader's letters as if used by them

parts.note: a kitty is a pet cat

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the eastern letter, enclosing it
wandering means straying about, so the letters of a merchant move into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat is taken by a travelling merchant round an eastern region looking for buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges A MERCHANT, and 'round' wraps those letters around E.
explanation.definitionFit: The area from which a shop, school or hospital draws its users is named this, so it is a region for customers.

clue.text: Pedantic phoney's love dismissed by the Queen

indicators.note: one letter is sent away and the royal pair takes its place, a swap

parts.note: a phoney is a fake, a pretender, so one who is hypocritical
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A fussy hypocrite's lover is sent packing by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed by' replaces the O of HYPOCRITICAL with ER, the late Queen's royal cipher (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excessively critical nitpicks over small details, which is what a pedant does.

clue.text: Literature that's lost the plot?

parts.note: writing with no storyline because it deals with fact rather than invented stories

explanation.surface: Literature that has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost the plot' is slang for going crazy; here it means writing that has no story plot at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual writing such as history and biography has no invented storyline, so it has no plot.

clue.text: Away from home, time to wear dead crumpled old hat

parts.note: a team playing away is out, not at home

indicators.note: the letters of dead are worn around time, enclosing it
crumpled means crushed out of shape, so the letters of dead are jumbled

explanation.surface: Travelling, someone dons a dead man's battered old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges DEAD into DAED, and 'to wear' puts T inside, making DATED. 'old hat' looks like the crumpled headgear, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale or out of fashion, no longer current.

clue.text: Rasp needed for cunning plan

definitions.meaning: a rasp is a harsh breathy sound, as from a chest infection
a clever scheme or trick, in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone with a hoarse voice needs a clever scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a whistling breath sound and British slang for a clever scheme or dodge.

clue.text: Belt one aristo's got on

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
I is the Roman numeral one
a toff is British slang for an upper-class person, an aristocrat

explanation.surface: Someone thumps an aristocrat who has climbed aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on well with someone on first meeting is an idiom with exactly this sense of getting along.

clue.text: Growth of pleasure — well, that's endless

parts.note: fun means enjoyment or pleasure

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the flowing word is dropped

parts.note: to well up is to gush, to flow out

explanation.surface: A growth of pleasure that just keeps welling up without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last letter of GUSH, leaving GUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms and moulds are organisms that grow, and a fungal growth is a common phrase.

clue.text: On going in opposite directions, best to be persistent

indicators.note: going here means going the other way, so the word on is turned back

parts.note: taken as written before it turns
north and south are opposite compass directions, N and S
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going in opposite directions to be the best and persistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' is the reversal signal on 'On'; 'opposite directions' gives the two compass points north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops is relentless or persistent.

clue.text: Sleazy club founder gets attack from on high

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub
to founder is to fail badly, and to bomb is to flop

explanation.surface: The founder of a seedy nightclub comes under a fierce attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founder' looks like a noun for the club's creator, but it is the verb meaning to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft that plunge steeply before releasing their bombs make an assault from above.

clue.text: Gold and green veg and other food grown here

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A list of produce, gold and green vegetables, all grown in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry. The definition points to fruit, the other food, grown in a place where chard is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees such as apples and pears are planted in this piece of land, so fruit is grown there.

clue.text: Like one who scoffs when folk get heated?

definitions.text: Like one who scoffs when folk get heated?

parts.words: Like one who scoffs when folk get heated
parts.note: scoffing means wolfing down food, and folk getting heated means people being cooked, so this describes a man-eater

explanation.surface: Describing someone who sneers when people lose their tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' suggests mockery and 'heated' anger, but read literally it is someone eating people who have been cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating human flesh is the defining habit of a people-eater, hence this adjective.

clue.text: A university occasionally copied, held up as sound

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means raised, read bottom to top
occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of copied is taken

explanation.surface: At a university, some work was copied from time to time and held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes OID from COPIED, and 'held up' turns it to DIO in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to recorded or transmitted sound, as in the soundtrack of a programme.

clue.text: Caught Romeo escaping from relation in blue

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the letter escapes, leaving the story word without it

parts.note: a relation is an account or story, a yarn
Romeo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: Romeo is caught fleeing a relative while feeling blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' suggests a relative but means a told story, a YARN; 'escaping from' removes R from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish-blue colour, one of the printing inks, is a shade of blue.

clue.text: Said to be obsessed with study in retirement

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it, even obsessed

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the study word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be obsessed with study now they have retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' is the reversal signal: retiring means drawing back, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to utter or recite in a chanting voice, so the past tense means spoken or said.

clue.text: Revered figure, royal, almost due to go walkabout

indicators.note: a walkabout is a wandering ramble, so these letters wander into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of due is cut

explanation.surface: A revered royal is about to go on a walkabout among the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DUE to DU, and 'to go walkabout' rearranges ROYAL plus DU. A royal walkabout is when a member of the royal family mingles with the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin Mary is venerated by Christians, a revered figure known by this title.

clue.text: Scruff takes ecstasy, seeing little sleep ahead

indicators.note: the short sleep comes in front of the drug letter

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A scruffy type takes ecstasy, foreseeing a short sleep to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' puts NAP in front of E.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff of the neck is its back, so scruff is another word for the back of the neck.

clue.text: Bed one rises to go to

definitions.text: Bed one rises to go to

parts.words: Bed one rises to go to
parts.note: a flower bed you climb up to, on top of a building, rather than a bed you go to at night

explanation.surface: A bed that someone gets up in order to go to.
explanation.walkthrough: One normally goes to bed and rises from it; here the bed is a planted one you rise to by going upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grown on top of a building sit in beds reached by going up.
